heard: A monster solar storm missed, erasing our modern world by nine days. On July 23, 2012, the sun launched a massive Carrington-class plasma eruption. This blast traveled at over 2,000 kilometers per second, four times faster than normal. It achieved this record speed because an eruption four days earlier had cleared its cosmic path. A direct hit would have crippled global power grids and water pumps, costing over $2 trillion. Instead, NASA's Stereo-A spacecraft in deep space safely recorded the entire blow. Physicist Pete Riley calculated a 12% chance a similar disaster strikes Earth each decade. We survived only because the erupting region of the sun was no longer pointed directly at us.
